key_insight: Patient-specific tricuspid valve finite element models can reproduce valve closure using clinical 3D echocardiography supplemented with ex vivo human tissue measurements.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports valve mechanics analysis and future repair-planning tools while identifying modeling inputs that require careful uncertainty assessment.
method: Manually segment 3D transesophageal echocardiography and automatically construct finite element models with synthetic chordae.
Assign leaflet thickness, chordal insertion density, and tissue properties using ex vivo human measurements.
Simulate closure through shape matching and force-based chordal-length adjustment; assess segmentation and parameter sensitivity.
evidence_signal: Across ten functionally competent human valves, per-valve median geometric errors were 0.55–0.95 mm against image-derived surfaces, with coaptation covering 20–42% of leaflet area.
watch_item: Evaluation was limited to functionally competent valves; segmentation variability strongly affected coaptation, and pathological-valve repair planning remains unvalidated.
paper_title: Patient-specific Modeling of the Tricuspid Valve from 3D Transesophageal Echocardiography
